scope: Two retained real Lichess roots and five deliberately constructed adversarial variants. These are development checks, not an independent accuracy sample. A withheld certificate is not a claim that the whole position is losing or free of tactics.

cases.judgement: Nd7 creates a real rook attack plus checking fork. Against Bd3, taking the rook allows Qe2 mate; Nf6+ must replace that unsafe witness. The genuine primary theme should survive.
Rb1+ prepares a checking knight fork; blocking with Rc1 instead loses that rook. Preserve the root preparation and the actual later fork.

The extra queen is deliberately unprotected. After Bb1, taking a rook loses that queen; even the checking fork must account for this off-square liability. Reject the old all-defence certificate, not all possible ways White might win.

Rbxa6 takes a bishop before the fork; after Kf8 and Nxh5, Rxa1 reduces that line's local residual to 70 cp. But White can instead answer Rbxa6 with Rxa6: the moved original rook victim can be captured by an ally. Retain the genuine double threat using this connected alternative, not the unsafe fork witness.
Bxe5 threatens the queen while preventing Nf6+. The old rook-taking witness ignores the queen loss; material elsewhere and the defender's counterattack matter.
An advanced passed pawn is a concrete resource after the advertised payoff. The bounded preparation must not certify a gain while silently ignoring promotion.
The checking sequence wins a rook but allows the other rook to capture Black's queen. Check and fork geometry cannot certify the preparation while ignoring the off-square queen.
